cues.en: My talk is called, what has my compiler done for me lately? Unbolting the compiler's lid, which is the longest and most complicated title I've seen. Titles, it turns out, are very hard. So, why am I up here staring back at you all? It's definitely a question I'm asking myself at the moment. As Jason, in his wonderful introduction, has said, my name has rather unexpectedly become a noun and a verb, which has led to some extraordinarily surreal conversations this last week.
cues.zh: 我的演讲题目是“编译器最近为我做了什么？揭开编译器的盖子”，这是我见过最长最复杂的标题。事实证明，起标题真的很难。那么，我为什么站在这里看着大家？这也是我现在正在问自己的问题。正如 Jason 在精彩的介绍中所说，我的名字出乎意料地变成了一个名词和一个动词，这过去一周引发了一些极其超现实的对话。

cues.en: I've not only had people come up to me and introduce themselves as if we're old friends, and I'm looking at them smiling, going, who are you? And then they say, thank you for compiler explorer, which is amazing. Or I've been in conferences, and people have been talking about Godbolt, and how there are those neurons in your brain that are always background process listening out for your own name, and I'm just looking around like this. So it's been very, very, very surreal. So thank you for the very warm reception. But I'd like to talk a little bit about me, just so you know how it is that I came to.
cues.zh: 不仅有人走过来像老朋友一样介绍自己，我笑着看他们，心想你是谁？然后他们说，谢谢你做了 Compiler Explorer，太棒了。或者在会议上，人们谈论 Godbolt，说你大脑里总有那些神经元在后台监听自己的名字，我就这样四处张望。所以真的非常非常超现实。谢谢大家的热烈欢迎。但我想先谈谈我自己，让你们了解我是怎么。

cues.en: come up with this idea for Compiler Explorer. Like a lot of people, I'm sure, I started a long time ago programming on these 8-bit computers here, which is, as Jason alluded to, still kind of a hobby of mine, still hacking around on the 6502 and the Z80. After a few years of trying to write my own games, that meant writing stuff in assembly, because that's the only way you could get anything done performantly back in those days.
cues.zh: 想到 Compiler Explorer 这个点子的。和很多人一样，我很早就开始在这些8位计算机上编程，正如 Jason 提到的，这仍是我的爱好，还在折腾 6502 和 Z80。尝试写自己的游戏几年后，那意味着用汇编写东西，因为那时候这是获得性能的唯一办法。

cues.en: I moved over to the ARM processor. I sort of hung on to the 8-bit era rather too long, and then when the leap came, I made it all the way to 32-bit. And back in those days, there wasn't a version of GCC for my computer, so I was stuck still writing assembly code. I even ended up writing a whole IRC chart client in assembly, complete with windowing and scripting and everything built in, just because that was pretty much the only option open to me. So when I finally was introduced to C,
cues.zh: 后来我转向 ARM 处理器。我在8位时代停留得太久了，当跳跃来临时，我一路跳到了32位。那时候我的电脑上没有 GCC 版本，所以我仍然困在写汇编代码中。我甚至用汇编写了一个完整的 IRC 聊天客户端，带窗口、脚本等所有功能，因为那几乎是我唯一的选择。所以当我终于接触 C 时，

cues.en: I considered it a bit of a macro programming, sorry, a macro assembler. It was kind of like one of these things was an annoyance. It got in the way of me writing the assembly that I wanted to write. But when I got to university and discovered that, oh, wow, suddenly it's very dark in here. Nobody's falling asleep, right? When I got to university, I realized that the only way that I could actually write software that would run on more than just my one-on computer that I had, I realized I had to learn C. And at that point,
cues.zh: 我把它当成一种宏编程，抱歉，宏汇编器。它有点像一种烦人的东西，妨碍我写想写的汇编。但当我上大学后发现，哦哇，突然这里好暗。没人睡着吧？上大学时我意识到，要写出能在我那台电脑之外运行的软件，我必须学 C。那时，

cues.en: things moved on and eventually C++ too. That led to me getting a job in the games industry where I spent 10 happy years, still kind of on the fence between writing assembly code and C code and maybe a bit of C++. After that I had a dabble in writing C++ tools. So for those people who work on C++ tools, I have a huge amount of sympathy for you. The language is absolutely dreadful and it's the worst thing to have to parse.
cues.zh: 事情继续发展，最终也学了 C++。这让我进入游戏行业工作了愉快的10年，仍在写汇编、C 和一点 C++ 之间摇摆。之后我尝试写 C++ 工具。所以对于那些做 C++ 工具的人，我非常同情你们。这门语言极其糟糕，是最难解析的东西。

cues.en: So if you see anyone from, like, JetBrains or anything like that, I give them a good, firm handshape or anyone from Eclipse. I then worked at a small internet startup. And then I moved on to DRW, which is the company I'm at now, where I do sort of low latency stuff. So you can sort of say I've already stayed pretty close to the metal. So what about this talk? It's an amazing opportunity to speak to so many C++ developers. And I thought to myself, what am I going to do with this time? What do I love? What do I want to tell people about?
cues.zh: 所以如果你见到 JetBrains 之类的人，或者 Eclipse 的人，我都会给他们一个有力而坚定的握手。后来我在一家小型互联网创业公司工作。之后我去了 DRW，也就是我现在所在的公司，在那里做些低延迟相关的东西。所以可以说，我一直都相当贴近底层。那这次演讲呢？能对着这么多 C++ 开发者讲话，是个绝佳机会。我就想，我要拿这段时间讲什么？我爱什么？我想告诉大家什么？

cues.en: I love assembly. You probably realized that from the last few slides. So I want to make sure that you guys are happy and aren't scared at looking at assembly. It's a useful thing to do, and you should be doing it. Not all the time, and I'm not saying that you should go out and learn how to write assembly code or that you should even ever write assembly code, but you should be able to look at the output of your compiler and with some confidence know what it's doing. And when you do that, you'll appreciate how much work has gone into the compiler.
cues.zh: 我爱汇编。你们可能从刚才那几页幻灯片就看出来了。所以我想确保你们看得开心，不会害怕看汇编。这是件有用的事，你们应该去做。不是一直做，我也不是说你们要出去学怎么写汇编代码，甚至不是说你们应该写汇编代码，但你们应该能看着编译器的输出，并且有一定把握地知道它在做什么。等你这么做时，就会体会到编译器里投入了多少工作。

cues.en: and how clever the compiler is. There's a lot of glamorous features that come out in the language, you know, all these new meta classes, Herb's also meta classes, ideas, reflection is coming, and all the template meta programming tricks that you can do with the compiler. That's awesome, but that's all in the front end. It's very important as well that the code that comes out the other end, the thing that actually is going to run on the computer is efficient. Well, first is correct, and secondly is about as efficient as it can be. So the outline of this talk is that...
cues.zh: 以及编译器有多聪明。语言里出现了很多很炫的功能，你知道，这些新的元类，Herb 也在讲的元类、想法，反射也要来了，还有你能用编译器做的各种模板元编程技巧。那很棒，但那些都在前端。同样非常重要的是，另一端出来的代码，也就是真正要在计算机上运行的东西，是高效的。首先得正确，其次要尽可能高效。所以这次演讲的大纲是……

cues.en: I'm gonna give you a little bit of a back story as to how Compiler Explorer came about. I wanna give you a very quick x86 assembly overview. I'm gonna ask the question, what has my compiler done for me lately? Which is just to say, I'm gonna look at some of the optimization, some of the cool optimizations that compilers do. Now, of course, these are all gonna be slide examples, so they're all totally contrived, but hopefully you'll get, it'll wet your appetite for it. And then I'm gonna talk a little bit about what happens when you type into my website, what's happening behind the scenes to give you your
cues.zh: 我先讲一点 Compiler Explorer 是怎么来的背景故事。我想快速带你们过一遍 x86 汇编。我要问一个问题：我的编译器最近为我做了什么？也就是说，我会看一些优化，一些编译器做的很酷的优化。当然，这些都是幻灯片里的例子，所以全都完全是刻意构造的，但希望你们能明白，它会勾起你们的兴趣。然后我会稍微讲讲，当你在我的网站里输入内容时会发生什么，幕后发生了什么，才能把你的

cues.en: code results back in front of you. So in 2012, a friend and I were at work and we were discussing whether or not it would be possible for us to start turning on the C++OX flag or the C++11 flag on the compiler and start using some of these new features that were coming through. Things like rangefors, auto variables, things like that. And being a high frequency trading shop, we can't just say to everyone, go ahead, just use whatever cool new feature is available. We need to make sure that we haven't done any harm.
cues.zh: 代码结果重新呈现在你面前。2012 年，我和一个朋友在工作时讨论，我们是否可能开始在编译器上打开 C++0x 标志或 C++11 标志，并开始使用一些当时正在出现的新功能。比如 range-for、auto 变量之类的。作为一家高频交易公司，我们不能只对大家说，去吧，随便用什么现成的酷炫新功能。我们需要确保没有造成任何损害。

cues.en: So we concocted an example bit of code like this, which is, as you can see, it's just taking a vector by reference, vector of integers by reference, and it's just summing them all up. Yes, this could just be std accumulate, I know, but bear with me. And we wondered that this traditional way of writing it, that is just a looping over an iterator by using an index into that iterator, looping over a container, I'm sorry, by using an index into that container, that would be how we'd write it before. We wondered whether or not we could replace it with a much nicer code.
cues.zh: 于是我们编了这样一段示例代码，如你所见，它只是通过引用接收一个 vector，一个整数 vector 的引用，然后把它们全部加起来。是的，我知道这直接用 std::accumulate 就行，但请先听我说。我们想知道，这种传统写法——也就是用索引遍历迭代器，抱歉，是用索引遍历容器——以前我们会这么写。我们想知道能不能把它换成更漂亮的代码。

cues.en: here, just using, you know, rangeful. We've been bitten before by other languages because some managed languages in particular that we had some experience with will construct iterators in order to iterate over a container like that. And that would generate garbage and ultimately things would go on behind the scenes. Obviously C++ doesn't have garbage to worry about, but we just didn't know. We would like to check, you know, we should test these things. So which one of these is better than the other? And that would be kind of like the leg into us me talking about
cues.zh: 这里只是用了 range 写法。我们以前被其他语言坑过，尤其是一些托管语言，我们有过经验：它们为了遍历这样的容器会构造迭代器，于是会产生垃圾，背后还会做一堆事。显然 C++ 不用担心垃圾回收，但我们就是不知道。我们想确认一下，这种事应该测试。那么这两个哪个更好？这大概就相当于引子，让我接下来讲

cues.en: how Compiler Explorer came about. And if my clicker works, we'll go to the next one. So before I get into a whole bunch of assembly, we're going to sort of tell you, give you at least enough information to know about how to read assembly. I'm going to give you a big warning here. It's really beguiling to stare at the output of your compiler and start to kid yourself that you can see what it's doing and know instinctively that this is better than that or this other thing is best or like there are fewer instructions and so it must be faster, things like that.
cues.zh: Compiler Explorer 是怎么来的。如果我的翻页笔能用，我们就进入下一页。所以在我开始讲一大堆汇编之前，我至少要先给你们足够的信息，了解怎么读汇编。这里我要重点警告一下：盯着编译器输出看，然后开始骗自己说你能看出它在干什么，凭直觉就知道这个比那个好、另一个最好，或者说指令更少所以一定更快——这种事真的很诱人。

cues.en: If any of you were in here before for Chandler's talk, he gave just a tiny glimmer of the kind of complicated things that are going on inside a modern processor. And you really can't predict. So while you can obviously develop an intuition about what's going on, you should always measure. You should definitely use something like Google Benchmark or one of the other benchmarking libraries that's out there that have done their best to try and make it as bulletproof as possible, although micro-benchmarks have their own problem. Or you can, a quick shout out to Fred if he's in the audience somewhere.
cues.zh: 如果你们之前在这里听过 Chandler 的演讲，他稍微展示了现代处理器内部那些复杂机制的一丝微光。你真的无法预测。所以，虽然你显然可以培养出对发生什么的直觉，但永远应该测量。你绝对应该用 Google Benchmark，或者现有的其他基准测试库，它们已经尽力做到尽可能可靠，尽管微基准测试也有自己的问题。或者你可以——如果 Fred 在观众里，顺便向他提一句。

cues.en: for his site, Quick Bench, which is an awesome online tool that allows you to check out two different snippets and compare the performance. Again, using Google Bench by behind the scenes, but also in an interactive online way. So let's talk a little bit about x86. Well, first of all, I guess, how many of you compile for x86 platforms by raise of hands? Good. I had this terrible fear that suddenly everyone's going to say, no, no, we do ARM now. All right, who does ARM?
cues.zh: 也就是他的网站 Quick Bench，一个很棒的在线工具，可以拿两段代码片段对比性能。背后同样用 Google Bench，但还能在线交互式地做。那我们稍微聊聊 x86。首先我想问，有多少人是为 x86 平台编译的？请举手。很好。我刚才特别怕突然所有人都说：不不，我们现在都做 ARM 了。好，谁做 ARM？

cues.en: Arm predominantly. There's a few hands. What about 32-bit x86? Is that still being targeted? A smattering? Anyone got a more exotic processor that you regularly build for? Oh, yes, a PDP-11, right? All right. Well, that gives me at least some legs. It would be really embarrassing now if suddenly I had to invent another architecture to talk about, but we're going to talk about x86 and specifically x86-64.
cues.zh: 主要是 ARM。有几个人举手。那么 32 位的 x86 呢？还有人针对它做开发吗？有零星几个？有人有更冷门的、经常要编译目标的处理器吗？哦，有，PDP-11，对吧？好，这至少让我有话可说了。如果讲到这里我突然又得发明一种新架构来讨论，那可就太尴尬了，不过我们要聊的是 x86，确切地说是 x86-64。

cues.en: We don't need to know too much about it. All you need to know, it has registers. These are 64-bit values, and there are 16 of them. Back in the 32-bit version of the chip, there were only eight of them with these funny names, AX, BX, CX, DX, and all these things, and some of them have special meanings as well, but for the most part, you can think of them as general purpose variables. Luckily, when AMD decided to extend out to a 64-bit version, they added in eight more registers, which was handy.
cues.zh: 我们不需要了解太多。你只需要知道，它有寄存器。这些是 64 位的值，一共有 16 个。回到 32 位版本的芯片，那时只有 8 个寄存器，名字还很奇怪：AX、BX、CX、DX 之类的，其中一些还有特殊含义，但在大多数情况下，你可以把它们当作通用变量。幸运的是，当 AMD 决定扩展出 64 位版本时，他们额外增加了 8 个寄存器，这很方便。

cues.en: and instead of inventing new funny names, they just called them the far more sensible R8 to R15. Those are where the integers are stored. That's your integer variables inside the processor. There are some other registers, the XMM registers, or YMM and ZMM, depending on which revision of the processor you've got. Any of your floating point operations will happen in there, and any sort of packed operations will happen in those registers, too. But by and large, and at least for this talk, I'm not gonna talk about those registers. The only other thing you need to know is that there's an ABI. There's a way that...
cues.zh: 而且他们没有发明新的奇怪名字，而是直接用了合理得多的名字：R8 到 R15。这些就是存放整数的地方，也就是处理器内部的整型变量。还有一些其他寄存器，XMM 寄存器，或者叫 YMM、ZMM，取决于你处理器的版本。所有浮点运算都会在那里进行，各种打包（packed）操作也在那些寄存器中进行。但总的来说，至少在本次演讲中，我不会讲那些寄存器。你唯一还需要知道的是，有一个 ABI。有一种方式让……

cues.en: functions talk to each other, and that's by convention. And that convention is that when I call a function, the arguments of that function will be an RDI, RSI, RDX, and then some other registers. And then if you're returning a value, an integer value that is, you're gonna leave it in RAX. And there are rules about which registers you're allowed to overwrite and which registers you have to preserve, but if you're not writing assembly, you don't need to know. So that's kind of like our ABI for talking.
cues.zh: 函数之间相互交流，这是靠约定实现的。这个约定是：当我调用一个函数时，该函数的参数会放在 RDI、RSI、RDX，然后是一些其他寄存器。而如果你要返回一个值——确切地说是整数值——你会把它放在 RAX 里。还有一些规则规定哪些寄存器可以随意覆盖、哪些必须保留，但如果你不写汇编，就不用管这些。这大致就是我们用来……

cues.en: between functions. Now registers, as I said, are 64-bit, but they have all these different names. So I've given RAX as an example here, but this is true also for RBX, RCX, all the other ones, and even R8 through R15. If we put an R at the beginning, we mean the whole 64 bits of the register. If we say EAX, we mean a 32-bit version of the register, and we just get the bottom 32 bits. And for complicated reasons, if you write to EAX, it zeroes out the top 32 bits.
cues.zh: 在函数之间交流的 ABI。寄存器，正如我所说，是 64 位的，但它们有各种不同的名字。我这里以 RAX 为例，不过这对 RBX、RCX 和其他所有寄存器都适用，甚至包括 R8 到 R15。如果在开头写 R，就是指整个寄存器的 64 位。如果写 EAX，指的是 32 位的版本，只取低 32 位。而且由于一些复杂的原因，写入 EAX 时，高 32 位会被清零。

cues.en: That's not true of AX, AH, and AL, which are these names for the bottom 16 bits and then the two bottom bytes, which are kind of legacy. I mean, this is kind of how Intel have maintained backwards compatibility right back up to the, I think, the 8088 by having essentially just adding on these, widening the registers, and giving them new names each time. Once you've got registers, you have to do things with them. So that's when we finally get to talk about instructions.
cues.zh: 但 AX、AH 和 AL 不一样，它们是低 16 位以及最底下两个字节的名字，属于历史遗留。我的意思是，Intel 基本就是这样一直维持向后兼容的，我想可以追溯到 8088——本质上就是每次加宽寄存器，然后给它们起新名字。有了寄存器之后，就得对它们做点什么。所以现在我们终于要讲到指令了。

cues.en: So instructions can take anywhere between zero and three operands. And unlike Chandler's talk, I'm using the Intel syntax here. So by, yeah, exactly. God, I had a whole routine done for like tabs of these spaces and things, but I didn't realize it was going to get that much of a clap. So yeah, by show of hands, who uses Intel syntax when they're looking at assembly? OK. And who uses the AT&T syntax? Oh. Oh, good.
cues.zh: 所以指令可以带零到三个操作数。和 Chandler 的演讲不同，我这里用的是 Intel 语法。所以，对，正是。天哪，我本来为制表符、空格这些东西准备了一整套段子，但没想到能收获这么多掌声。那好，举手示意一下，看汇编时谁用 Intel 语法？好。谁用 AT&T 语法？哦。哦，很好。

cues.en: I thought I was going to make some enemies today, but this is why GCC Explorer, Compiler Explorer, listen to me, Compiler Explorer has Intel assembly by default because it makes sense. And because I grew up, and everyone else is wrong, I'm sorry. No, because I grew up, again, with ARM and 6502, and they all have the destination on the left-hand side. So if you see anything on my slides, the destination of the instruction is going to be the left-hand parameter. So operations can be things like call, return.
cues.zh: 我本以为今天会树些敌，但这就是为什么 GCC Explorer，等等，Compiler Explorer，听我说，Compiler Explorer 默认用 Intel 汇编，因为这合理。因为我从小就用它，而其他人都错了，抱歉。不，还是因为我从小接触的是 ARM 和 6502，它们的目标操作数都在左边。所以如果你在我幻灯片上看到什么，指令的目标操作数就是左边那个参数。所以操作可以是 call、return 这类东西。

cues.en: add, subtract, exclusive or, and, or all those kind of bits and pieces. And then, sort of uniquely to x86, well not uniquely, specific to CISC type machines, like x86 is, those destination and source registers, sorry, things that are up there, don't have to be registers. They often are, but they can also be references to memory. And being...
cues.zh: 加法、减法、异或、与、或，诸如此类。然后，算是 x86 独有的，呃不，不是独有，而是 CISC 类机器特有的，比如 x86，那些目标和源寄存器——抱歉，是上面那些东西——不一定是寄存器。它们经常是，但也可以是对内存的引用。而且……

cues.en: as complicated as it is, the reference to memory can actually be more than just a memory address. We get this huge layer of options at the bottom here. We get like a base, which is a constant. We can pick another register and say add that register to it. And then we can also pick yet another register and add a multiple of one, two, four, or eight to it. Obviously this is handy for things like arrays because you want to have a pointer to the beginning of the array and then you want to get like the i-th element. You want to put i in one of the registers and then you're going to multiply it by one, two, four, eight to kind of move it forward that number of bytes.
cues.zh: 尽管很复杂，内存引用其实可以不只是内存地址。这里底部有一大层选项。比如有一个基址，是个常量。我们可以再选一个寄存器，把那个寄存器加到基址上。然后还可以再选一个寄存器，把它乘以 1、2、4 或 8 后加进去。显然这对数组这类东西很方便，因为你想要一个指向数组开头的指针，然后想取第 i 个元素。你会把 i 放进某个寄存器，再乘以 1、2、4、8，让它向前移动相应字节数。

So it's a bit like a VM within a VM, although much lighter weight.
cues.zh: 它会被分发到我后台众多实例中的一个。那些实例是运行 Ubuntu 的虚拟机。而在这些虚拟机里，正如我告诉你们的，是洋葱层，有 Docker 镜像。所以 Docker 就是那种非常轻量级的容器技术，它允许你把数据打包在一起，并有点像是在命名空间里运行进程，这意味着它只能看到计算机的一部分。所以它有点像虚拟机里的虚拟机，虽然轻量得多。

cues.en: That gives me a certain amount of protection from all the crazy code you guys put in the site, not taking down the whole thing. cues.zh: 这能在一定程度上保护我，不至于因为你们往站点里塞的各种疯狂代码而把整个东西搞挂。它也让我能确保，本地运行的二进制文件和要部署到站点上的完全一致。所以大多数时候，我更新站点不会把它弄坏。有很长一段时间，我其实会把所有编译器镜像都构建进那些 Docker 镜像里。

cues.en: started getting less fun when you get 40 or 50 gigabytes worth of compilers, and you try and build a node, sorry, a Docker image for it, and then you have to try and push it to all of the nodes, and it takes like 10 or 15 minutes for a node to start up because it has to pull down all this data before it can even start. cues.zh: 所以这些 Docker 镜像有点像小虚拟机，你会 shell 进去，我会准备一堆命令，比如 sudo apt-get install gcc dash 等等等等之类的。那很好，非常方便。但后来我发现，我最初为 Ubuntu 11 放到站点上的那些编译器正在被弃用，它们没法在 GCC 12、14 或 16 上安装。所以我得留着一个容器，只是因为它里面有某个我想保留的古老编译器。而且我想确保你们到处分享的那些 URL 始终

cues.en: going to work, which is a whole other story. URLs are forever. Forget any kind of radiation thing. It's like URLs stick around absolutely forever. cues.zh: 都能用，这又是另一回事了。URL 是永久的。别管什么辐射半衰期了，URL 会永远留在那儿。所以现在它们都是通过这些 Docker 镜像构建的。我花了不少时间学习构建编译器的良好实践，并把这些实践整理成了规范。这些都放在我的网站上，我应该在最后放个链接。它们放在 Docker 镜像里构建，就是因为这样我能获得可复现构建，这是我很在意的东西。

cues.en: anyone else to be able to clone this down and be able to build the same compiler that Compiler Explorer is using. cues.zh: 让其他人也能把它克隆下来，并构建出 Compiler Explorer 正在使用的同一个编译器。更关键的是，其实我构建好之后就把它们扔到 S3 上，并标记为公开。我老是收到 Amazon 的邮件，因为最近有很多人发现自己在 S3 上有公开信息，而他们并不是故意的。可我确实是故意的。它们公开的原因是，你其实可以跑一个 shell 脚本，只要硬盘空间够，就能把 40 GB 的开源编译器倒进你的硬盘里，这很酷，因为这样你就能跑自己的本地实例

So I'm glad to say I've met up with Andrew and some of the other Microsoft folks who are going to help me, and we're hoping to get some proper
cues.zh: 比如，如果你不想把代码发给我，就可以跑自己的本地 Compiler Explorer 实例。这些是开源的。Intel 很好心地也给我提供了 ICC 的许可证，放在别的地方了。微软的编译器目前也是通过 Wine 跑的，这多少算是我承认自己不太懂怎么管理 Windows，仅此而已。所以我很高兴地说，我见了 Andrew 和其他一些微软的人，他们会帮我，我们希望能很快给 Compiler Explorer 带来一些正经的

cues.en: support for the Windows compilers into Compiler Explorer soon. So that's a really exciting thing that's coming up. Oh! Thank them. Thank them. And, you know, security. Well, I only got an email this morning actually from someone who thinks they've hacked my site, and maybe they have, I don't know. Turns out a compiler is a gigantic security hole waiting to happen. It's a huge attack vector. Compiler writers are awesome, as I think I've already said enough times.
cues.zh: 对 Windows 编译器的支持。所以这是接下来很令人兴奋的事。哦！谢谢他们，谢谢他们。然后，你懂的，安全性。其实我今天早上刚收到一封邮件，有人说他们黑了我的站点，也许真黑了，我不知道。结果发现，编译器就是一个等着发生的巨大安全漏洞。它是个巨大的攻击面。编译器作者很厉害，我觉得我已经说过很多次了。

cues.en: They're not really security experts, and they don't have to be, right? They're on a trusted system. But I had no idea how many ways there were to inject code into a compiler. You think the compiler just builds the code. I'm not actually executing it, right? But GCC has a plugin architecture. You can supply minus F plugin and point it at something which is a load as a dynamic library. So if you can cause the compiler to crash, but having written the file somewhere, and then my cleanup code doesn't work immediately, then you might be able to guess the path of it, and then
cues.zh: 他们并不是真正的安全专家，也不必是，对吧？他们处在可信系统上。但我完全没想到，往编译器里注入代码的方式有这么多。你以为编译器只是构建代码，并不会真的执行它，对吧？但 GCC 有插件架构。你可以传 -fplugin，指向某个会作为动态库加载的东西。所以如果你能让编译器崩溃，同时已经把文件写到某个地方，而我的清理代码又没有立刻生效，那你也许能猜出它的路径，然后

cues.en: do another compile with minus F plug-in equals and then you're in. Only happened once. Also behind the scenes, GCC uses something called specs files, which I don't claim to understand, but seems to be part of the processes, the many, many...
cues.zh: 再用 -fplugin= 编译一次，你就进来了。只发生过一次。另外在幕后，GCC 用了叫 specs 文件的东西，我没法说我懂它，但它似乎是流程的一部分，很多很多……

cues.en: pipelined processes that comprise a compilation, you know, from the preprocessor through CC1 plus through the AS assembler and all that kind of stuff. And essentially, it's a set of shell commands to run. And, of course, you can say, actually, I'd like you to use my specs file over here. And, again, you're back in the same world, where as long as you can write a file somewhere on the disk that says run, I don't know, netcat or something, then, you know, you're in. Now, I sort of...
cues.zh: 构成一次编译的流水线进程，从预处理器到 cc1plus，再到 AS 汇编器之类的。本质上，它就是一组要运行的 shell 命令。当然，你可以说，其实我想让你用我这里的 specs 文件。于是你又回到同一个世界：只要你能在磁盘某处写一个文件，内容是运行，比如说 netcat 之类的东西，那你就进来了。现在我有点……

cues.en: started down a route of trying to harden everything, and then eventually I came to the conclusion that there's just no way I can make it completely bulletproof. And so I've accepted that the principle of what's the worst that can happen, it should apply. And that is, you could hack one of my nodes, and you can take down the Docker instance, and even if you don't get out of the Docker container, the worst you can do is stop it from running, and then something else will come and kill the process, and it'll start up again. So hopefully that's not too bad.
cues.zh: 开始走上把所有东西都加固的路线，后来我得出结论：根本没办法做到完全无懈可击。所以我接受了“最坏能坏到哪去”的原则，应该适用。也就是说，你可以黑掉我的一个节点，你可以把 Docker 实例搞挂；即使你逃不出 Docker 容器，最坏也只能让它停止运行，然后别的东西会来杀掉进程，它又会重新启动。所以希望这还不算太糟。

cues.en: Even if you escape the Docker sort of CH root and namespace jail, which I told is possible, you're in a VM which has no privileges to anything. I'm aware that it's being recorded and someone's gonna email me and say, oh, this is not actually true, but oh well.
cues.zh: 即使你逃出了 Docker 那种 chroot 和 namespace 牢笼——我说过这是可能的——你也在一个对任何东西都没有权限的虚拟机里。我知道这正在被录像，会有人给我发邮件说，哦，这其实不对，但就这样吧。

cues.en: Anyway, so Docker protects me in some ways from this, and I experimented for a long time using LD preload tricks, which is a unique specific thing where you can force a dynamic library to be loaded before an executable is run, and then you can replace some of the system routines. So I have a little bit of code that...
cues.zh: 总之，Docker 在某些方面保护了我。我长期试验过 LD_PRELOAD 技巧，这是一种很独特的手段：你可以强制在可执行文件运行前加载一个动态库，然后替换一些系统例程。所以我有一小段代码，……

cues.en: basically replaces open and read and all that kind of stuff, and just has a blacklist and whitelist of all the different files that I was allowing the compiler to read, and that was my way of preventing people from doing like, hash include slash etc password, ha ha ha, which is essentially the kind of thing that had people try first. Turns out though, the compiler needs to read etc password, because it wants to know which user's running it, and I thought, well, we'll allow that. And then it was, oh, now it's trying to read proc CPU info, and I'm like, well, that's a bit dodgy.
cues.zh: 基本上替换 open、read 之类的函数，并维护一个黑名单和白名单，列出我允许编译器读取的所有不同文件。这就是我防止别人做类似 #include /etc/passwd 哈哈哈那种事的方式，这也正是人们最先尝试的东西。但结果发现，编译器需要读 /etc/passwd，因为它想知道是哪个用户在运行它。我想，行吧，这个我们允许。然后变成，哦，现在它又想读 /proc/cpuinfo，我就想，这有点可疑。

cues.en: Oh, why should I let it read the proc file system? And it's like, well, because people want to type march equals native, and how else is the compiler going to find out what CPU it's running on? And so on and so forth. And before I knew it, everything was basically fair game for the compiler. I just threw my hands up and said, well, sod it. cues.zh: 哦，凭什么要让它读 proc 文件系统？事实是，因为大家想输入 march=native，不然编译器怎么知道自己跑在什么 CPU 上呢？如此等等。不知不觉间，所有东西对编译器来说都成了可以碰的。我只能摊手认栽，随它去吧。好，接下来我们应该聊聊那个前端，就是你看得见的部分。这里要再次狠狠感谢微软。Visual Studio Code 的编辑器是一个独立项目，用 JavaScript 写的，你可以直接拿来塞进自己的项目里。它太棒了，是一个功能齐全的编辑器。

And there are over 100 bugs that have citations to compiler explorer links. And people use it to sort of bisect quickly. You can just drop.

To Bjarne's point in the opening keynote, you know,

cues.en: teaching C++ and making sure people understand how to write this code and understanding the processes that we go through when we write code is important and it's nice that I feel it can compile this work and help with that. In fact, it's on the beta site or beta site. So if you go to godbolt.org slash B-E-T-A,
cues.zh: 教授 C++，确保人们理解如何写这些代码，理解我们写代码时所经历的过程，这很重要；而我觉得它能补充这项工作并有所帮助，这很好。快速预告一下即将推出的东西，我总把顺序说反。有一个 CFG，也就是控制流图查看器，很快就会推出。事实上，它已经在 beta 站点上了。所以如果你访问 godbolt.org/B-E-T-A，

cues.en: then you'll see that there is a new icon on the far right-hand side of the assembly pane. You can click and drag, and you get a view that shows all how the different basic blocks interact. cues.zh: 然后你会看到汇编窗格最右侧有一个新图标。你可以点击拖动，就会得到一个视图，显示不同基本块之间是如何交互的。我还想统一所有语言，所以你注意到了，很多人说它叫 gcc.godbolt.org 并不合适。它应该就叫 godbolt.org。嗯，其实它真应该叫 compilerexplorer.com，但现在没人会让我改名了。

cues.en: for America's first space disaster. We wrote two more words into our vocabulary as mission controllers, tough and competent. cues.zh: 要对美国首次太空灾难负责。作为任务控制人员，我们在自己的信条中写下了两个新词：坚毅与胜任。坚毅意味着我们绝不再推卸责任，因为我们将永远对自己的所作所为负责。胜任意味着绝不再把任何事视为理所当然。我们将永不停歇地学习，从现在起，任务控制团队必须做到尽善尽美。因为作为一个团队，我们绝不能失败。还有一件事。
